scope: Four independent SDKs locally compute state vectors, Pauli expectations and selected-angle derivatives. This does not expose each upstream SDK in full.

setup.command: node scripts/setup-paper-tools.mjs pennylane-differentiable deepquantum-differentiable tensorcircuit-differentiable mindquantum-differentiable
setup.result: All four explicitly prepared environments checked against frozen dependency locks; Python 3.11 for MindQuantum and 3.12 for the other three.

checks.evidence: strict schema, registry declaration, provenance mismatch rejection, worker errors, credentials excluded, thread forwarding and cancellation recovery
Each SDK has seven independent dense and exact parameter-shift cases; actual stdio MCP tools/list plus explicit/default calls and invalid parameter rejection.

checks.check: ESLint for all new JavaScript in this group
Python source compilation for all new Python in this group

limitations: Harness-wide execution and independent domain review are separate aggregate integration evidence, not claimed by this SDK-only record.

DeepQuantum retains native fixed-H complex64 construction error after conversion to float64; maximum observed state error is about 6.85e-8 and Jacobian error about 5.34e-8 in these cases. No output was clipped or normalized.
DeepQuantum photonic, Gaussian, Fock, MPS and distributed methods are not exposed by this qubit differentiation action.
TensorCircuit 0.12.0 is pinned with JAX/JAXlib 0.4.38 and NumPy 1.26.4; TensorCircuit-NG and GPU execution are not covered.
PennyLane uses default.qubit only; MindQuantum uses mqvector without the MindSpore optional training framework.
Current host was tested. Other operating systems are represented by locked dependency distributions but were not executed here.

scienceRegression.reference: independent dense Pauli/gate algebra and exact parameter-shift derivative

cases.label: all-gates-three-qubits

result.bitOrder: lexicographic bitstrings q0 q1 ...; q0 is the leftmost, most significant bit

limitations: Ideal pure-state simulation from the all-zero state, with no noise or finite-shot sampling.
Each selected rotation angle is an independent parameter; no parameter sharing, optimization loop or hardware execution.
Probabilities and amplitudes are raw numerical outputs without clipping or renormalization; full state output grows as 2^numQubits.
This L1 execution does not establish scientific Acceptance or external-model validation.
